description:
Water features from the Overture base theme: ocean and inland water bodies, sourced from OpenStreetMap by translating its `natural` and `waterway` tags. For St. Louis that is above all the Mississippi River, plus the River des Peres, park lakes, and ponds, classified by `subtype` and `class`. Overture documents this data well: the [base theme guide](https://docs.overturemaps.org/guides/base/) covers what the theme models, how Overture builds it, and how to query it, and the schema reference gives every field of its feature type — [`water`](https://docs.overturemaps.org/schema/reference/base/water/).

Unlike everything else in this catalog, this is **not** City of St. Louis data: it comes from the [Overture Maps Foundation](https://overturemaps.org/), a collaborative project building open, interoperable map data for the world. This collection is a St. Louis extract of that global dataset — everything inside the city's bounding box, which also takes in the Illinois shore of the Mississippi (East St. Louis, Cahokia Heights) — included here to demonstrate how a city's open-data catalog can blend in other St. Louis-relevant open data alongside the city's own. The GeoParquet was extracted from Overture release 2026-07-22.0; the map tiles reference Overture's own global PMTiles for the same release, the tiles behind [explore.overturemaps.org](https://explore.overturemaps.org/).

table:columns.name: id
table:columns.description: Overture feature ID — per the schema, 'a feature ID. This may be an ID associated with the Global Entity Reference System (GERS) if—and-only-if the feature represents an entity that is part of GERS.' GERS IDs are intended to be stable across Overture's monthly releases, which makes this the key for attaching your own data to an Overture feature and for joining to any other GERS-enabled dataset. See the [GERS overview](https://docs.overturemaps.org/gers/).

table:columns.name: names
table:columns.type: struct<primary: string, common: map<string, string ('common')>, rules: list<element: struct<variant: string, language: string, perspectives: struct<mode: string, countries: list<element: string>>, value: string, between: list<element: double>, side: string>>>
table:columns.description: Names of the feature. `primary` is the most commonly used name; `common` holds translations keyed by IETF BCP-47 language tag; `rules` carries the variants that cannot be expressed as a simple common name (official, alternate, short), each optionally scoped to a `between` range along the geometry or to one `side` of a road. Schema reference: [names](https://docs.overturemaps.org/schema/reference/common/names/).

table:columns.name: subtype
table:columns.description: The type of water body, such as a river, ocean or lake. One of canal, human_made, lake, ocean, physical, pond, reservoir, river, spring, stream, wastewater, water. Schema reference: [water_subtype](https://docs.overturemaps.org/schema/reference/base/types/water_subtype/).

table:columns.name: class
table:columns.description: Further description of the type of water, a long list of values including river, stream, canal, ditch, drain, lake, pond, reservoir, basin, moat, swimming_pool, reflecting_pool, waterfall, spring and dock — translated from the OpenStreetMap `natural` and `waterway` tags. Schema reference: [water_class](https://docs.overturemaps.org/schema/reference/base/types/water_class/).

table:columns.name: sources
table:columns.type: list<element: struct<property: string, dataset: string, license: string, record_id: string, update_time: string, confidence: double, between: list<element: double>>>
table:columns.description: Per-property provenance. An array of source records, each naming the `property` it covers in JSON Pointer notation plus the source `dataset`, its `license` (an SPDX identifier where one is available; null means contact the data provider for terms), the `record_id` used, an `update_time`, and for ML-derived data a `confidence`. Every feature carries a root-level entry that is the default source for any property without a more specific one. Schema reference: [sources](https://docs.overturemaps.org/schema/reference/common/sources/).

table:columns.name: source_tags
table:columns.description: Attributes from the original OpenStreetMap feature passed straight through as a string-to-string map. The base theme lifts the tags it models into typed columns (`height`, `surface`, `wikidata` and the rest); whatever is left but still relevant stays here. Schema reference: [source_tags](https://docs.overturemaps.org/schema/reference/base/types/source_tags/).

table:columns.name: level
table:columns.description: Z-order of the feature, where 0 is visual level — a stacking hint for rendering overlapping features. Not an above-or-below-ground flag: negative values may still be above ground. Schema reference: [level](https://docs.overturemaps.org/schema/reference/common/level/).

table:columns.name: wikidata
table:columns.description: Wikidata item ID for the feature if available, as found on [wikidata.org](https://www.wikidata.org/) — the OpenStreetMap `wikidata` tag lifted to a top-level Overture property.

table:columns.name: is_intermittent
table:columns.description: Whether the feature is intermittent — dry for part of the year.

table:columns.name: is_salt
table:columns.description: Whether the feature is salt water.

table:columns.name: version
table:columns.description: Version number of the feature, incremented in each Overture release where the geometry or attributes of this feature changed. Schema reference: [feature_version](https://docs.overturemaps.org/schema/reference/common/feature_version/).

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: WKB geometry in EPSG:4326: polygons for water bodies, lines for watercourse centerlines, points for features such as springs. Geometries crossing the edge of the St. Louis bounding box were clipped to it, so the Mississippi and its Illinois-side channels stop at the box.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: Covering bounding box (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) for the row's geometry. Not an Overture schema column: Overture's own bbox was dropped and this one rebuilt by gpio during conversion, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network.

title: Overture Water

overture-water-tiles.title: Overture base theme (PMTiles, global)
overture-water-tiles.description: Overture's own release-pinned global vector tiles for the base theme, served from the Overture Maps Foundation's public bucket — not from this mirror, and not clipped to St. Louis. The styles select this collection's layers (water) from them.

styles/default.title: Water by subtype
styles/default.description: The Mississippi in deep blue, park lakes and ponds lighter, streams and canals teal — and the city's 374 swimming pools in purple. Lines (streams, drains) draw as lines, everything else as polygons.

styles/style-explorer.title: Explorer water
styles/style-explorer.description: One flat Explorer blue for every water feature — the basemap look.
